title: Shard aggregator rounding causing billing variance across routes
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Summary: We are seeing small but persistent invoice variances and per-route usage discrepancies caused by rounding behavior in the shard-level aggregator that consolidates token counts from edge shards. The aggregation currently applies per-shard rounding to token consumption before summing; under skewed request distributions this can produce systematic over- or under-counts for an org or route. This manifests as: 1) isolated routes showing +0.5-2% higher billed tokens versus sampled request traces; 2) occasional negative-looking corrections in daily billing reconciliations when route-level reconciler applies global normalization; 3) metering alerts triggered for customers on tight quotas.

Investigation notes: We reproduced locally by spinning up a 4-shard aggregator with synthetic load that sends fractional token attributions per-request (e.g., streaming partial tokens from long-lived websockets). After ~24h of staggered traffic we observed a 1.7% difference between aggregated per-shard rounded sum and a global single-pass tokenization baseline. Root cause: aggregator code (shard_aggregator.go) performs math.Round on per-shard floating counters when serializing to persistence, then sums integers. This was an optimization to reduce per-shard data size, but interacts poorly with frequent cross-shard routing of single logical requests (function-calls / tool-calls) which split attribution across shards and create rounding bias. Additionally, a compaction job later applies a normalization step that attempts to correct drift but only runs daily, causing transient-billed-overages.

Scope and impact: Affects hosted and dedicated edge shards when request splitting occurs (websocket streaming, multipart generation). Not triggered for single-shard pinning. Estimated customer-visible variance: 0.2% to 2.5% depending on traffic skew. Recent billing audit flagged four mid-market customers with anomalies; finance engaged. High priority because it impacts invoicing correctness and trust.

Repro steps: 1) Deploy local multi-shard aggregator with config shard_count=4 and enable_stream_partial_attribution=true. 2) Run synth workload that issues 10M tokens but splits single logical requests across 2-3 shards randomly. 3) Compare per-shard rounded-sum vs single-pass global counter stored in test harness. 4) Observe drift and reproduce correction when compaction job runs.

Temporary mitigations: 1) Disable per-shard rounding flag by runtime toggle to switch to high-precision per-shard counters (costs ~10% storage increase for metrics) — currently on staging. 2) Increase compaction frequency to hourly for affected customers (operational burden). Both mitigations available as short-term options until a proper fix is deployed.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Khatri: Initial report filed after Finance flagged invoice delta for ACME Corp. Included sample traces, anonymized request ids, and Grafana dashboard (https://grafana.redwood-inference.internal/d/billing/metering-variance).

2026-03-11 - Marcus Li: Reproduced locally and narrowed to rounding in shard_aggregator.go; created small test harness (repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/aggregator-tests/pull/14) that reproduces bias deterministically.

2026-03-12 - Marcus Li: Experimented with three fixes: (A) switch to exact integer micro-token accounting per-event, (B) carry fractional remainder in sharded serializations and flush to next record, (C) perform global reconciliation at write-time. A & B both eliminate bias; A increases metrics storage ~9%, B increases memory overhead ~2% and is more complex. Posted micro-benchmark results in doc: https://confluence.redwood-inference.internal/display/BILL/Shard+Rounding+Investigation

2026-03-12 - Priya Raman (Finance): Confirmed anomaly impacts 4 customers for Feb invoices; requested emergency mitigation to avoid March bills being wrong. Asked for clear rollback plan if mitigation causes side effects.

2026-03-13 - Marcus Li: Deployed runtime toggle to disable per-shard rounding to staging (toggle key: meter.aggregator.per_shard_rounding=false). Observed metrics increase and corrected billing sums across test customers. Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4217 (WIP).

2026-03-13 - Design (Evan Cho): Noted monitoring implications — dashboards need an additional panel showing pre- and post-compaction delta so SRE can triage regressions. Filed DES-240 for dashboard change.

2026-03-14 - Marcus Li: Proposal: Implement option B (carry fractional remainders) as default fix — lower operational cost than A and keeps storage increase minimal. Plan: patch aggregator serialization to include "remainder" field (integer micros) and ensure idempotent merging. Will add migration that replays recent shards to apply remainder corrections. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4229 (branch: fix/shard-remainder).
2026-03-14 - Security (Anita Gomez): Quick review indicates no direct security impact; remainder field is non-sensitive. No full security review required.

2026-03-14 - Marcus Li: Next steps: 1) Land unit + integration tests that simulate cross-shard logical requests, 2) run canary deploy in staging for 48h with billing comparison, 3) schedule production rollout with feature flag and finance approval, 4) add alert rule that fires if per-route reconciliation delta > 0.5% after rollout. Assigned QA to replicate customer audit cases.

2026-03-14 - Aisha Khatri: Added follow-up tasks for retrospective: (a) update runbook for compaction jobs, (b) add automated daily reconciliation report for top-20 customers, (c) evaluate whether other aggregators (quota, usage-credits) have similar rounding logic.
qa_plan: Unit tests that create deterministic cross-shard requests, integration test using aggregator-tests harness with 48h run, staging canary that compares billed tokens vs baseline, and a finance-verified reconciliation run for the 4 impacted customers before full rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge PR behind feature flag; 2) Canary 5% of edge traffic for 24h; 3) If delta < 0.25% and no errors, increase to 50% for 24h; 4) Full rollout and disable old rounding toggle; 5) Run reconciliation job and notify Finance. Backout: flip toggle back and revert PR if regressions observed.
postmortem_notes: Will follow up with a short postmortem after rollout covering decision rationale (A vs B), storage/ops cost tradeoffs, and timelines to add permanent dashboards and automation.
